description.value: A simultaneous tDCS-fMRI study examined whether anodal vmPFC stimulation attenuated anger and aggression during an anger-infused Ultimatum Game in healthy participants.

value: Our primary hypothesis was that active anodal relative to sham tDCS during the aiUG would lead to increased vmPFC activity, particularly during the processing of angering unfair offers, thereby increasing acceptance rates of unfair offers and decreasing levels of self-reported anger following the task.

White-matter and cerebrospinal-fluid time courses and motion parameters were later included as nuisance regressors.

description.value: Participants played the responder in an anger-infused Ultimatum Game.

description.value: Fair offer condition: participants received 12 offers in which the responder was offered 40–50% of the total stake, accompanied by non-confrontational interpersonal messages, and decided whether to accept or reject each offer.

Medium offer condition: participants received 12 offers in which the responder was offered 25–35% of the total stake, accompanied by mildly provocative interpersonal messages, and decided whether to accept or reject each offer.

Unfair offer condition: participants received 12 offers in which the responder was offered 10–20% of the total stake, accompanied by intensely provocative interpersonal messages, and decided whether to accept or reject each offer.

spans.text: Each round began with a short fixation period

instructions.value: Participants were told that they were responding to randomly drawn offers supposedly made by previous participants. For each offer, they decided whether to accept or reject it; acceptance meant both players gained their allocated money, whereas rejection meant both players lost it. They were told that the three participants accumulating the largest sum of accepted offers would receive their actual monetary earnings.

stimuli.value: Thirty-six predetermined monetary offers were presented: 12 fair offers offering 40–50% of the total stake, 12 medium offers offering 25–35%, and 12 unfair offers offering 10–20%. Stakes ranged from 20 to 30 Israeli New Shekel. Each offer was accompanied by the initials of a putative proposer and a short written interpersonal message: non-confrontational for fair offers, mildly provocative for medium offers, and intensely provocative for unfair offers.
